display.title: Episode 510: The Three Loaves of Bread
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi asks Tzivos Hashem soldiers to help friends join a yeshiva, then tells how King Shlomo explained the mystery of an old woman's lost loaf of bread.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi describes Tzivos Hashem as a worldwide army whose missions build character and Ahavas Yisroel. One example: a soldier who attends a yeshiva helps a friend or relative join one too, and children are invited to write in to try a yeshiva for a day. After the Hakochainik march, a second-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school recites the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: an old woman tells King Shlomo that she gave two of her three fresh loaves to starving beggars, and the wind then carried the third loaf out to sea. Shlomo HaMelech tells her to trust that whatever Hashem does is for the good. Soon a foreign king arrives: his ship was sinking until a loaf of bread plugged the hole, and he had vowed half his wealth to charity. The old woman bakes an identical loaf, and the fortune goes to her. The show closes with a listener's letter about kibbud av va'em, Shabbos candle-lighting times, and a gift for girls who begin lighting Shabbos candles.
display.lesson: Whatever Hashem does is for the good, even when we cannot understand it yet; trust Him and be patient.
